Damian Lillard is carrying the offensive load for Portland with 18 points and 1 assist, while Georges Niang has chipped in 13 points for the Warriors. Despite Lillard's output, Golden State's supporting cast is vastly outplaying Portland's stars through the first two quarters.

The Warriors are completely dominating the game on the margins, highlighted by a staggering 36-7 advantage in bench points and a +6 rebounding differential. Golden State is also punishing Portland on the offensive glass with a 0.391 OREB%, while Portland is struggling to take care of the ball with 10 turnovers leading to a poor 0.90 AST/TO ratio. 

4. SECOND-HALF OUTLOOK
The Warriors are locked in with an 87.0% win probability and are projected to close this out with a 9-point victory. To secure the win, Golden State must maintain their 0.375 three-point shooting efficiency and keep exploiting Portland's weaker 0.294 perimeter defense.
